questions.prompt: How should ordinary letters in a search pattern be handled?

choices.label: Try every child edge even for an ordinary letter.
choices.feedback: An ordinary character must match exactly; only a dot permits multiple choices.

choices.label: Ignore the letter and stay at the same trie node.
choices.feedback: An ordinary character must match exactly; only a dot permits multiple choices.

choices.label: Follow the edge for that exact letter.
choices.feedback: An ordinary character must match exactly; only a dot permits multiple choices.

questions.prompt: What should a dot in the search pattern do?

choices.label: Match only a literal dot stored in a word.
choices.feedback: A dot matches exactly one arbitrary letter, so each recursive branch advances by one pattern position.

choices.label: Match any number of characters, including none.
choices.feedback: A dot matches exactly one arbitrary letter, so each recursive branch advances by one pattern position.

choices.label: Try each character child for that one position.
choices.feedback: A dot matches exactly one arbitrary letter, so each recursive branch advances by one pattern position.

questions.prompt: After every pattern character is matched, what confirms success?

choices.label: The trie contains any word of any length.

choices.label: The current node has at least one child.
choices.feedback: Matching a prefix alone does not prove that a complete word with this pattern length was stored.
